rows.meaning: Standing body height; not skill or automatic defensive impact.
Arm-span measurement supporting reach geometry.
Measured overhead reach. If unavailable, estimate with uncertainty; do not add height and wingspan again as extra contest bonuses.
Mass relevant to contact and inertia; not equivalent to functional strength.
Rate of gaining movement speed, without the ball.
Attainable movement speed over distance.
Without-ball lateral movement, braking and redirection capacity. Do not infer this directly from screen-navigation success. Separate lateral/COD observations may be retained beneath this family.
Capacity to apply/resist force. Contact leverage technique remains a separate skill.
Capacity to maintain or regain bodily control. Learned footwork and decision quality are separate.
Reach added by jumping. Standing reach + jump determines potential coverage; timing determines how effectively it is used.
Ability to sustain repeated workload before execution deteriorates.
Rate of recovering from exertion during rest/lower-intensity periods. Not injury recovery or developmental resilience.
Shot preparation and accuracy from a catch at reference three-point distance. Not assumed equal to pull-up ability.
Dribble pickup, shot footwork and accuracy from a live dribble at reference distance.
Shooting while settling from substantial off-ball movement. Movement and catch labels can overlap; use a conditional model, not both full bonuses.
Midrange catch preparation and accuracy.
Midrange live-dribble shot execution.
Midrange execution after off-ball movement; sparse evidence should remain visibly uncertain.
Uncontested free-throw shooting skill. Release speed is not an input to this talent.
How quickly the player can prepare and release an appropriate shot without losing their usual mechanics. Actual release window also depends on the shot type and contest.
Ability to preserve mechanics as distance increases beyond a reference shot. Derived usable range also requires sufficient accuracy and willingness; this is not a second universal accuracy bonus.
Control, angle, touch and hand use on close attempts. Does not establish ability to get to the rim.
Converting floaters and short-paint touch shots; distinct from explosive paint access.
Takeoff coordination and ball control when a dunk is physically available. Reach/vertical determine availability, not this skill alone.
Timing and coordination to receive and finish airborne chances. Combines with receiving and the appropriate finish, without treating every assisted basket as a lob.
Securing and preparing to use an incoming pass, including difficult deliveries.
Protecting the ball, adjusting and preserving finish control through contact. Strength contributes separately to effective contact tolerance.
Ball control through changes of hand, direction, speed and dribble moves. Does not itself confer physical speed.
Protecting possession against pressure. Must directly influence ball-loss risk at comparable exposure.
Footwork, fakes, counters and deception that create shot or attack space. Complements dribble manipulation, rather than measuring the same moves twice.
Choosing/maintaining attack angles, using the defender's hip, changing pace and exploiting lanes.
Recognizing when to shoot, drive, post, reset or move the advantage. Specific passing reads live in F01-F09.
Technique to gain and retain useful receiving/post position.
Footwork, fakes and counters to create a post advantage.
Hooks and other post-specific release techniques. A generic layup or jumper from the post still uses its own shot skill, not two full accuracy ratings.
Timing and body/ball placement that draw legal contact during an available attack. Does not create free throws without an attack and defender interaction.
Timing, deception, route choice and presenting a usable receiving window. Speed is supplied by physical tools; frequency by tendencies/assignments.
Timing and disguising relocation, using screens and arriving prepared to shoot. The subsequent shot uses S01-S06 as appropriate.
Screen angle, placement, legal positioning and contact technique. Body size/strength do not automatically establish competence.
Recognizing when to hold, re-screen, slip, roll or pop. Passing after the catch uses the relevant passing family.
Reading shot trajectory, finding a route and establishing offensive rebounding position. Not simply observed offensive rebounds.
Reading misses and securing advantageous defensive rebounding position.
Finding an opponent, gaining legal leverage and maintaining a seal. Can create a teammate's rebound.
Timing and controlling/tipping a reachable ball. Reach, jump and strength are supplied separately.
Stance, angles, footwork and spacing to keep an assignment contained. Effective containment also needs movement tools.
Absorbing, redirecting and resisting contact through technique; physical strength and balance remain distinct.
Approach, body positioning and route technique around screens. Not another copy of lateral speed.
Establishing depth/angle relative to the rim, ball, attacker and roller. Specifically interior, not every kind of defensive positioning.
Timing, hand/body placement and controlled vertical execution to challenge a shot. Shot context selects the relevant response; blocks are possible outcomes, not a second skill bonus.
Identifying help responsibilities, tags, switches and the next threat early enough to act.
Executing useful gap, denial, tag and recovery starting positions away from the primary matchup. Distinct from interior positioning, with legitimate overlap in evidence.
Approaching under control, managing angle/distance and avoiding an easy blow-by or foul. Physical travel speed is separate.
Reading handler cues, passing windows and movement routes. It informs several tasks, but does not duplicate their execution skills.
Timing and placement of hands to dislodge or take the ball.
Executing interceptions and deflections of reachable passes. Recognition and reach also matter.
Maintaining awareness of ball, assignment and coverage responsibilities. Not identical to intelligence or voluntary effort.
Maintaining legal contact/contest execution in difficult actions. Intentional tactical fouls are a separate decision.
Recognizing and delivering useful coverage calls. Proposed team-coordination skill, not a personality/leadership rating or a universal defense bonus. Evidence may be scouting-led.
Identify the next useful continuation or ball reversal
Deliver the continuation accurately and on time
Read the seal, denial and entry window
Place the entry where the receiver can secure/use it
Read roller availability, coverage and the gap
Deliver through the gap at the receiver's useful height/pace
Identify aerial availability and help timing
Place trajectory/timing for a usable aerial finish
Read the advantage after the screener catches in space
Deliver the appropriate pass from that short-roll situation
Read help commitment and the perimeter outlet
Deliver accurately while driving or exiting the drive
Identify a useful weak-side window beyond nearer receivers
Deliver across the defense with appropriate pace/trajectory
Read cutters, doubles and outlets from the post
Deliver out of post position, including constrained body angles
Recognize an available advantage upcourt
Deliver an accurate moving/long advance or outlet
Conditional action distribution given the available options.
Spatial attempt preferences, including side/region tendencies. Not regional accuracy.
Catch, pull-up and movement attempt preferences conditional on opportunity.
Willingness to attempt contested, early or difficult shots; game state modifies the decision.
Preference to advance or attack before the defense is set.
Preference to retain the ball and continue probing rather than move it.
Willingness to attempt difficult/high-reward deliveries. Not pass recognition or accuracy.
Tendency to seek touches/initiations. Actual usage is limited by coach plans, teammates and opportunity.
How often the player seeks a cut when opportunities arise.
How often the player seeks another receiving/shooting location.
Conditional mix of screen actions and follow-ups.
Preference to pursue a miss versus recover defensively. Skill and coach strategy determine whether this is useful.
How the player allocates attention between collecting and securing space for others. Not a choice to abandon all rebounding.
Attempt appetite at a given apparent opening. Separate from execution and anticipation.
Willingness to leave an assignment, stunt or commit to help within the scheme.
Choice to jump, contest conservatively or preserve position. Technique governs the consequences.
Offensive, defensive and transition workload choices. Conditioning limits sustainability; high offensive usage is not automatic proof of defensive laziness.
Whether the player seeks contact or avoids it while attacking. Foul-drawing and contact finishing are separate skills.
